profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, named "Verizon North Las Vegas" and tagged telecom=data_center, is located in North Las Vegas, Clark County, Nevada. Verizon Communications is a real, major, publicly traded US telecommunications company headquartered in New York City, formed through the 2000 merger of Bell Atlantic and GTE, but its legacy wireline network only serves as the incumbent local carrier in nine eastern states, and Nevada is not among them. That makes a traditional Bell-heritage telephone central office an unlikely explanation for a Verizon-attributed building here, with a Verizon Wireless mobile switching center or other nationwide cellular network facility a more plausible category, since Verizon Wireless operates infrastructure across the entire country regardless of Verizon's separate wireline footprint. This building's outline was originally imported from a Microsoft open building-footprint dataset, with its name, operator, and telecom tags added afterward by an OpenStreetMap contributor whose sourcing basis could not be independently verified this session. No address, capacity figures, or independent news coverage could be located, since search-tool quota was exhausted. A separate, unrelated "Verizon" record also exists elsewhere in Clark County, roughly 8.5 miles away, confirmed to be a genuinely distinct location rather than a duplicate of this one, though its own specific function is equally unconfirmed. This entry is filed as an honest, unresolved case, most plausibly Verizon network infrastructure rather than a commercial colocation data center, without asserting fabricated specifications.

reading.body:
No specifications are published for this facility. Verizon Communications divested its commercial colocation business to Equinix in 2017 and does not publish technical capacity or power figures for its own network infrastructure. This entry appears in OpenStreetMap as a telecom facility in North Las Vegas, but the sourcing basis cannot be independently verified and research avenues are exhausted.

The facility's actual function is unclear. Verizon's wireline operations do not serve Nevada, making a traditional telephone exchange unlikely. A Verizon Wireless mobile switching center or cellular network facility is more plausible, since Verizon Wireless operates nationwide infrastructure regardless of wireline footprint. This would make the site operational backbone for Verizon's own traffic rather than third-party colocation capacity.

Without published power capacity or IT load specifications, this facility cannot be assessed as a factor in AI infrastructure scaling. Nevada has only two facilities with published megawatt figures in the world as indexed here, totaling 10.37 MW, and neither is this one. The state supports 26 mapped data centers in aggregate, but almost all operate without disclosed capacity metrics.
